solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flying stunt cut — nothing in it

indicators.note: in it says the zero is placed inside the word for cut

parts.note: to lop is to cut off, as a branch
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A pilot's aerobatic manoeuvre gets cut short, with nothing left in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerobatic manoeuvre in which the aircraft flies a full vertical circle is a classic display trick.

clue.text: Excessively serious English composer's appearing in public

indicators.note: appearing in says the English composer's pieces sit inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
Thomas Arne, English composer of Rule, Britannia!, with the 's adding S

explanation.surface: An English composer's piece is performed openly.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne, English composer of Rule, Britannia!, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Too earnest means taking things far too seriously.

clue.text: One calling to support unfinished harbour vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath the other piece
unfinished says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a port is a harbour
a ringer is one who rings, calls by phone or chimes bells

explanation.surface: A caller props up a half-built harbour where boats wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship after 'harbour', but it is a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bowl with a handle, used for porridge or soup, is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: British soldiers began without resolution, going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means the letters are read right to left
without in its old sense of outside: the word for began goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: began means started
RES is the standard abbreviation for resolution, as on a screen or in a council

explanation.surface: Soldiers set off without any determination, heading westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking; 'going west' reverses the whole of STARTRESED.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the British 7th Armoured Division, famed for the North African campaign of the Second World War.

clue.text: Good form last month nothing unusual

parts.note: Dec, short for December, the year's final month
O as zero
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Last month's behaviour was nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is a dated British word for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper, polite behaviour is good form, observing the expected etiquette.

clue.text: Avoiding work whilst engaged in plays

definitions.note: shirking or malingering, an old naval phrase

indicators.note: plays means the preceding letters move about freely, as in play in a mechanism, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a theatre swing is an understudy, who takes the starring role when on stage

explanation.surface: Someone shirking work while busy acting on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' looks like theatre to go with 'engaged', but it signals that 'whilst engaged in' is rearranged; the phrase is an old naval idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means malingering or skiving, pretending to be ill or busy to dodge duties.

clue.text: Exceed time limit for survey

definitions.meaning: to go beyond the allotted time
to look over or review quickly

explanation.surface: Going past the deadline for an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to overrun a schedule and to glance quickly through something.

clue.text: Not straight like part of SW London

parts.note: as means in the manner of, like
Kew, home of the botanical gardens, is in south-west London

explanation.surface: Something crooked about a corner of south-west London.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is a district of south-west London known for its botanic gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked or awry, out of line, is this adjective.

clue.text: Cheerful address to a lad overheard

indicators.note: overheard says the word is heard, not seen, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: sonny is a familiar way to address a young boy

explanation.surface: A cheerful greeting to a boy picked up by an eavesdropper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright, happy disposition is described like fine weather.

clue.text: Withdrawal of touching drawing

parts.note: re, the Latin-derived preposition, means concerning or about
traction is the act of drawing or pulling a load

explanation.surface: A sketch is taken back because it was too affecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking back a statement or claim is a formal withdrawal of it.

clue.text: Almost broke cover

indicators.note: Almost says the word for broke loses its final letter

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

explanation.surface: Someone nearly penniless reaches for a cover story.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is everyday British slang for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer of an animal or fruit is its natural covering.

clue.text: One refusing to acknowledge some yarn

definitions.meaning: a person who disavows or contradicts something
the unit measuring the fineness of silk or nylon yarn, familiar from hosiery labels

explanation.surface: Someone won't admit to a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who denies is literally this, and the same word names the weight unit used for tights and stocking yarn.

clue.text: Present Queen holds a view that's disguised

indicators.note: holds says the slang word wraps round the scrambled letters

parts.note: queen is slang for a gay man, so gay stands in for it

indicators.note: disguised means rearranged out of recognition, signalling an anagram of the two words before

explanation.surface: The monarch keeps a perspective that is concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' is not ER here but dated slang for a gay man; 'that's disguised' rearranges A VIEW to IVEAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A free gift handed out, often as a promotion, is something given away as a present.

clue.text: Stripper bringing wrong tone into a country house

indicators.note: into says the scrambled letters go inside the words for a country house

parts.note: a grange is a country house with farm buildings

indicators.note: wrong says these letters are set out incorrectly, in a new order

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer takes an off-key note into a manor house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripper' is a chemical that strips leaves, not a dancer; 'wrong' gives ENTO, which 'into' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The defoliant sprayed during the Vietnam War stripped vegetation from the jungle.

clue.text: Rough projection of Conservative newspaper

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative in British politics
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A Tory tabloid makes a crude forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep jagged outcrop of rock juts out roughly from a hillside.

clue.text: Merchant to supply white wine

indicators.note: read as the adverb from supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A dealer is going to provide a bottle of white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb supple-ly, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated Burgundy appellation producing Chardonnay, one of the great white wines.

clue.text: Noble not up for launch preparation

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
the opposite of up is down

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who's not out of bed gets ready to set off.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbered sequence of seconds before a rocket lifts off is the launch preparation.

clue.text: Rogues copy Hitchcock character

parts.note: a repro is a reproduction or copy
Norman Bates is the motel keeper in Hitchcock's Psycho

explanation.surface: Villains imitate a figure from a Hitchcock film.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprincipled people of bad character are rogues and scoundrels.

clue.text: Walk by brother to gather berries

parts.note: B abbreviates brother
a ramble is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: Taking a stroll with a sibling to pick blackberries.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, the word for a blackberry bush means to go picking blackberries.

clue.text: Second fiddle is one making a hum

parts.note: to tinker is to fiddle about with something

explanation.surface: A second violinist produces a drone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hum' is British slang for a bad smell, not a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives off a bad smell is a source of stench.

clue.text: Busy with leader of party out for change

indicators.note: for change says the collected letters are to be reordered
leader of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Occupied with a party head being ousted to make way for something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' rearranges P (the leader of party) with OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being occupied with some activity, often mischief: what are you doing now?

clue.text: Some trust a gnat eventually to stop moving

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rely on a midge eventually coming to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or an economy that ceases to flow or develop becomes still and inactive.

clue.text: Small tree French writer's climbed

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbed means the letters go upward, read bottom to top

parts.note: Albert Camus, French author of The Outsider

explanation.surface: A French author has scaled a little tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a shrub or small tree of the cashew family, grown for its autumn colour and spice.

clue.text: Drying equipment is lighter after top's removed

indicators.note: the top in a down clue is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: fairer means paler, lighter in colour

explanation.surface: Laundry kit is lighter once its top comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse or rack for drying laundry indoors.

clue.text: Detain working student

definitions.meaning: to confine someone, especially in wartime, without trial
a trainee or student gaining work experience, especially in medicine

explanation.surface: Holding back a student who has a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to imprison without charge; the noun is a junior trainee doctor or work-placement student.

clue.text: Nag man to adopt a change of direction

indicators.text: to adopt a change of direction
indicators.note: left becomes right: the L, a direction, is swapped for R, the other direction

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: Pester a man into turning round.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) is replaced by R (right) in MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old or worn-out horse is a nag, and a female horse is a mare.

clue.text: Depressed on holiday, son collapses

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the next piece

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
feeling down is being depressed
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A miserable lad on holiday falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanical failures or nervous collapses are both known by this plural noun.

clue.text: Helper overcoming fear finds machine taking money

indicators.note: overcoming read literally: the word for helper comes over and around the word for fear

parts.note: a carer looks after someone sick or elderly
dread is great fear

explanation.surface: An assistant beats their anxiety and finds a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The device a shop uses to take payment from a debit or credit card is this terminal.

clue.text: They may have it after motion, one's recollected

definitions.text: They may have it after motion

indicators.note: read as re-collected, gathered again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something remembered after a motion, which may belong to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' means re-collected, i.e. rearranged, not remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: After a parliamentary motion the Speaker declares 'the ayes have it' or the opposing votes have it.
